scope: Exodus 1–4, all 100 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 1–4.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the opening link to Genesis and the family households while making the following list part of the sentence.
verses.before: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob, each with his household:
verses.after: These are the names of Israel’s sons who came to Egypt with Jacob, each with his household:
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt with Jacob, each with his household:

verses.rationale: Retains the first four sons in source order and uses list punctuation rather than a separate sentence.
verses.before: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
verses.after: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah;
verses.tsw_comparator: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

verses.rationale: Preserves the next three names without rearranging them into birth order.
verses.before: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
verses.after: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin;
verses.tsw_comparator: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s paired names as the list concludes.
verses.before: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.after: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.tsw_comparator: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

verses.rationale: Retains the seventy and Joseph’s separate location without harmonizing the wording of this descent total to Genesis 46’s household explanation.
verses.before: All the descendants of Jacob were seventy persons; Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.after: Jacob’s own descendants numbered seventy in all. Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the descendants of Jacob were seventy persons; Joseph was already in Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold passing of Joseph, brothers, and generation as the narrative transition.
verses.before: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
verses.after: Joseph died, and so did all his brothers and that entire generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the accumulation of fertility, teeming, multiplication, strength, and filling that recalls creation language.
verses.before: But the sons of Israel were fruitful and increased greatly; they multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, so that the land was filled with them.
verses.after: But the Israelites were fruitful and teemed with life. They multiplied and grew very strong, until the land was filled with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the sons of Israel were fruitful and increased greatly; they multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, so that the land was filled with them.

verses.rationale: Retains did not know rather than deciding whether the king lacked information or refused to acknowledge Joseph’s importance.
verses.before: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.after: Then a new king rose to power over Egypt, one who did not know Joseph.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparative claim as Pharaoh’s speech, not as an objective census supplied by the narrator.
verses.before: And he said to his people, “Look, the people of the sons of Israel are too many and too strong for us.
verses.after: He told his people, “Look at the Israelites! They are more numerous and stronger than we are.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to his people, “Behold, the people of the sons of Israel are too many and too strong for us.

verses.rationale: Retains Pharaoh’s calculated policy, feared alliance, and feared departure rather than changing his concern to expulsion.
verses.before: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and, if war breaks out, they join our enemies and fight against us and escape from the land.”
verses.after: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them so they do not multiply. If war breaks out, they might join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and, if war breaks out, they join our enemies and fight against us and escape from the land.”

verses.rationale: Names the agents and victims while retaining forced labor, its oppressive purpose, and both named storage cities.
verses.before: So they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with heavy burdens. They built for Pharaoh store cities, Pithom and Raamses.
verses.after: So the Egyptians put forced-labor overseers over the Israelites to oppress them with heavy burdens. They built the storage cities of Pithom and Rameses for Pharaoh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with heavy burdens. They built for Pharaoh store cities, Pithom and Raamses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the proportionate reversal and the resulting Egyptian dread.
verses.before: But the more they were afflicted, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And the Egyptians were in dread of the sons of Israel.
verses.after: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread. The Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the more they were afflicted, the more they multiplied and the more they spread abroad. And the Egyptians were in dread of the sons of Israel.

verses.rationale: Makes enslavement and ruthlessness explicit rather than describing ordinary employment.
verses.before: So they ruthlessly made the sons of Israel serve,
verses.after: The Egyptians worked the Israelites ruthlessly as slaves.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they ruthlessly made the sons of Israel serve,

verses.rationale: Retains bitter lives, construction and field work, and the deliberate repetition of ruthlessness.
verses.before: and made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and brick, and in all kinds of work in the field. In all their service they made them serve with harshness.
verses.after: They made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and brick and every kind of work in the fields. In all their labor, the Egyptians treated them ruthlessly.
verses.tsw_comparator: and made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and brick, and in all kinds of work in the field. In all their service they made them serve with harshness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named women and the Hebrew-midwives wording while noting the alternative midwives-to-Hebrews relationship.
verses.before: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,
verses.after: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one named Shiphrah and the other Puah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete birthstool image and the sex-specific killing order without euphemizing it.
verses.before: “When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool, if it is a son, you will put him to death, but if it is a daughter, she will live.”
verses.after: “When you help Hebrew women give birth,” he said, “look at the birthstool. If the baby is a boy, kill him. If it is a girl, let her live.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool, if it is a son, you shall put him to death, but if it is a daughter, she shall live.”

verses.rationale: Retains fear of God as the motive and the women’s active preservation of life.
verses.before: But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but let the male children live.
verses.after: But the midwives feared God. They did not do what the king of Egypt had told them; they kept the boys alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but let the male children live.

verses.rationale: Keeps both questions and the repeated kept-alive wording.
verses.before: So the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this, and let the male children live?”
verses.after: The king of Egypt summoned the midwives. “Why have you done this?” he asked. “Why have you kept the boys alive?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this, and let the male children live?”

verses.rationale: Presents the explanation as the midwives’ speech without asserting a biological ethnic distinction or declaring their account deceptive.
verses.before: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”
verses.after: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women. They are vigorous and give birth before the midwife reaches them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”

verses.rationale: Retains both divine kindness to the women and continued growth of the people.
verses.before: So God dealt well with the midwives. And the people multiplied and grew very strong.
verses.after: God treated the midwives well, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: So God dealt well with the midwives. And the people multiplied and grew very strong.

verses.rationale: Renders houses as households in context without specifying children’s numbers or an architectural reward.
verses.before: And because the midwives feared God, he made them households.
verses.after: Because the midwives feared God, he gave them households of their own.
verses.tsw_comparator: And because the midwives feared God, he made them households.

verses.rationale: Preserves the escalation to all Pharaoh’s people and does not insert Hebrew into an order whose wording leaves that qualifier unstated.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, “Every son that is born to the Hebrews you will cast into the Nile, but you will let every daughter live.”
verses.after: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, “Throw every newborn boy into the Nile, but keep every girl alive.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, “Every son that is born to the Hebrews you shall cast into the Nile, but you shall let every daughter live.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both parents’ Levite descent without importing their names from later chapters.
verses.before: Now a man from the family of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.
verses.after: A man from the house of Levi married a woman from that same house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now a man from the family of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi.

verses.rationale: Retains the mother’s seeing-good response and three-month concealment without substituting a later theological explanation.
verses.before: The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was good, and hid him for three months.
verses.after: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him for three months.
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was good, and hid him for three months.

verses.rationale: Keeps construction materials, deliberate placement, and reeds rather than describing the child as set adrift; the ark word is linked in a note.
verses.before: When she could hide him no longer, she took for him a basket made of bulrushes and coated it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the riverbank.
verses.after: When she could hide him no longer, she got a papyrus basket and coated it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child inside and placed it among the reeds at the edge of the Nile.
verses.tsw_comparator: When she could hide him no longer, she took for him a basket made of bulrushes and coated it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the riverbank.

verses.rationale: Retains the watching sister and her purpose without importing a name not supplied here.
verses.before: His sister stood at a distance to know what would happen to him.
verses.after: His sister stood at a distance to find out what would happen to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: His sister stood at a distance to know what would happen to him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the daughter, attendants, and specifically enslaved woman distinct, with the daughter initiating retrieval.
verses.before: Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe at the river, while her young women walked alongside the river. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maidservant to fetch it.
verses.after: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe in the Nile while her attendants walked along the bank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her slave woman to fetch it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe at the river, while her maidens walked alongside the river. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maidservant to fetch it.

verses.rationale: Preserves sight, crying, compassion, and explicit recognition of the child’s Hebrew identity.
verses.before: She opened it and saw the child. Look, the child was crying. She had compassion on him and said, "This is one of the Hebrews' children."
verses.after: She opened it and saw the child—a boy, crying. She felt compassion for him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She opened it and saw the child. Behold, the child was crying. She had compassion on him and said, "This is one of the Hebrews' children."

verses.rationale: Clarifies the sister’s offered action and retains the princess as the one for whom the nursing is arranged.
verses.before: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Will I go and call a nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?"
verses.after: His sister asked Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call a Hebrew woman to nurse the child for you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and call a nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?"

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise permission and the mother’s return without adding that the daughter recognized their relationship.
verses.before: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Go." So, the young woman went and called the child's mother.
verses.after: “Go,” Pharaoh’s daughter said. The young woman went and called the child’s mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Go." So, the young woman went and called the child's mother.

verses.rationale: Retains the promised payment and the repeated completed nursing action.
verses.before: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will pay you your wages." So, the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.after: Pharaoh’s daughter told her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay you.” So the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will pay you your wages." So, the woman took the child and nursed him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the adoption and Hebrew name explanation without treating it as an exhaustive historical etymology.
verses.before: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water."
verses.after: When the child had grown, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, “I drew him out of the water.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water."

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses’ kinship identification and repeated seeing; supplies no age beyond the source’s adulthood.
verses.before: In those days, when Moses had grown, he went out to his people and saw their burdens, and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his kin.
verses.after: Years later, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and saw their burdens. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days, when Moses had grown, he went out to his people and saw their burdens, and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his kin.

verses.rationale: Preserves looking for witnesses, killing, and concealment without excusing or exaggerating Moses’ action.
verses.before: He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
verses.after: He looked this way and that. Seeing no one, he struck the Egyptian dead and hid him in the sand.
verses.tsw_comparator: He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s identification of the wrongdoer and the question’s neighbor language.
verses.before: The next day, he went out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one in the wrong, "Why do you strike your fellow?"
verses.after: The next day he went out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you hitting your neighbor?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day, he went out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one in the wrong, "Why do you strike your fellow?"

verses.rationale: Preserves the challenge to authority, explicit prior killing, and Moses’ fear without making the man’s question a new threat.
verses.before: The man replied, "Who made you a prince and judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" Moses feared and thought, "Surely the thing is known."
verses.after: The man answered, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses was afraid. “What I did is known!” he thought.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man replied, "Who made you a prince and judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" Moses feared and thought, "Surely the thing is known."

verses.rationale: Keeps the death threat and both settle/sit actions in clear sequence.
verses.before: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat by a well.
verses.after: When Pharaoh heard about it, he sought to kill Moses. Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in Midian. There he sat down by a well.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat by a well.

verses.rationale: Retains seven daughters and both water-drawing and trough-filling tasks.
verses.before: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
verses.after: The priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came to draw water and fill the troughs for their father’s flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the women’s displacement and Moses’ rescue followed by practical care for the flock.
verses.before: The shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and helped them and watered their flock.
verses.after: Some shepherds came and drove them away. But Moses stood up, rescued them, and watered their flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and helped them and watered their flock.

verses.rationale: Keeps Reuel here rather than replacing it with Jethro from chapter 3.
verses.before: When they came to Reuel their father, he said, "How is it that you have come back so soon today?"
verses.after: When they returned to their father Reuel, he asked, “How did you get back so quickly today?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came to Reuel their father, he said, "How is it that you have come back so soon today?"

verses.rationale: Preserves the women’s identification of Moses as Egyptian and their emphatic report of his further help.
verses.before: They replied, "An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he even drew water for us and watered the flock."
verses.after: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they said. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They replied, "An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and he even drew water for us and watered the flock."

verses.rationale: Retains all three conversational movements while rendering eat bread idiomatically.
verses.before: He said to his daughters, "Where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread."
verses.after: “Where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man there? Invite him to eat with us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to his daughters, "Where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread."

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses’ agreement and the father’s giving of his daughter rather than inventing her consent or a wedding description.
verses.before: Moses agreed to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses his daughter Zipporah.
verses.after: Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave him his daughter Zipporah in marriage.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses agreed to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses his daughter Zipporah.

verses.rationale: Retains the foreigner/foreign-land repetition and name explanation tied to Moses’ displacement.
verses.before: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, saying, "I have been a foreigner in a foreign land."
verses.after: She bore a son, and Moses named him Gershom. “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land,” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, saying, "I have been a foreigner in a foreign land."

verses.rationale: Keeps elapsed time, the king’s death, and repeated slavery as the source of the cry; no claim that a new king improved conditions.
verses.before: It happened, in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned because of their labor, and they cried out, and their cry for help rose up to God from their hard labor.
verses.after: During that long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned under their slavery and cried out. Their cry for help rose to God from their slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: It came to pass, in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned because of their labor, and they cried out, and their cry for help rose up to God from their hard labor.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated divine subject and covenant/ancestor sequence rather than compressing the climax.
verses.before: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.after: God heard their groaning. God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

verses.rationale: Retains the terse final verb without supplying an object or reducing it to a generic statement that God cared.
verses.before: God saw the people of Israel, and God knew.
verses.after: God saw the Israelites. God knew.
verses.tsw_comparator: God saw the people of Israel, and God knew.

verses.rationale: Retains Jethro as named here, the flock, and the mountain designation without inventing a route or modern location.
verses.before: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led his flock beyond the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
verses.after: Moses was tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led his flock beyond the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves angel language and the simultaneous burning/not-consumed observation rather than explaining the manifestation.
verses.before: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and look, the bush was burning, yet it was not consumed.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire from within a bush. Moses looked: the bush was burning, but it was not being consumed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush was burning, yet it was not consumed.

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses’ decision to investigate and his question about the unconsumed bush.
verses.before: Moses said, “I will turn aside to see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”
verses.after: Moses said, “I must turn aside and look at this extraordinary sight. Why does the bush not burn up?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses said, “I will turn aside to see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the LORD/God alternation, doubled call, and response pattern familiar from Genesis.
verses.before: When the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
verses.after: When the LORD saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him from the bush, “Moses! Moses!” “Here I am,” Moses answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition, concrete sandal removal, and the stated holiness of the ground.
verses.before: Then he said, “Do not come near; take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”
verses.after: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take the sandals off your feet. The place where you are standing is holy ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Do not come near; take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”

verses.rationale: Retains the singular father followed by three ancestral identifications and Moses’ embodied fear.
verses.before: And he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
verses.after: He continued, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Moses hid his face because he was afraid to look at God.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic seeing, hearing, and knowing as distinct claims that answer chapter 2’s closing sequence.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters. I know their sufferings,
verses.after: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen my people’s suffering in Egypt. I have heard their cry because of their taskmasters. I know their pain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters. I know their sufferings,

verses.rationale: Preserves descent/ascent, Egypt’s hand, abundance image, and all six resident peoples rather than presenting the destination as empty land.
verses.before: and I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and broad land, a land flowing with milk and honey—to the place of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.after: I have come down to rescue them from Egypt’s hand and bring them up from that land into a good, spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the place of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and broad land, a land flowing with milk and honey—to the place of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated hearing/seeing assurance instead of deleting it as redundant.
verses.before: And now, look, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.after: Now the Israelites’ cry has reached me, and I have also seen how the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.

verses.rationale: Makes the commission’s movement clear and retains both my people and Israelites.
verses.before: Come, I will send you to Pharaoh that you may bring my people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt.”
verses.after: So go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Come, I will send you to Pharaoh that you may bring my people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the two-part task inside Moses’ question about himself.
verses.before: Yet Moses said to God, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt?”
verses.after: Moses asked God, “Who am I to go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said to God, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt?”

verses.rationale: Retains presence as the answer and makes the plural worshiping group explicit; the sign remains future rather than moved to the present bush.
verses.before: He said, “But I will be with you, and this will be the sign for you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.”
verses.after: “I will be with you,” God answered. “This will be the sign that I have sent you: when you bring the people out of Egypt, you all will serve God on this mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “But I will be with you, and this shall be the sign for you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”

verses.rationale: Makes the hypothetical dialogue audible while preserving the name question and ancestral relationship.
verses.before: Then Moses said to God, “If I come to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ what will I say to them?”
verses.after: Moses said to God, “Suppose I go to the Israelites and tell them, ‘The God of your ancestors has sent me to you,’ and they ask, ‘What is his name?’ What should I tell them?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to God, “If I come to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is his name?’ what shall I say to them?”

verses.rationale: Retains the familiar present rendering with the future alternative and link to I will be with you in a note; no doctrinal expansion is added.
verses.before: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” And he said, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
verses.after: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” Then he said, “Tell the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” And he said, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine name represented by LORD, the repeated ancestral titles, and the enduring memorial designation.
verses.before: God also said to Moses, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and thus I am to be remembered throughout all generations.
verses.after: God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD, the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever; this is how I am to be remembered from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: God also said to Moses, “Say this to the sons of Israel: ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever, and thus I am to be remembered throughout all generations.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic visitation as attentive action and both objects, linking it in apparatus to Joseph’s assurance without forcing identical syntax.
verses.before: Go and gather the elders of Israel together and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you and seen what is done to you in Egypt,
verses.after: Go and gather Israel’s elders. Tell them, ‘The LORD, the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, appeared to me and said, “I have surely attended to you and to what has been done to you in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go and gather the elders of Israel together and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you and seen what is done to you in Egypt,

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated complete resident-peoples list, suffering, ascent, and milk/honey image in the reported promise.
verses.before: and I promise that I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.”’
verses.after: I have promised to bring you up out of your suffering in Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: and I promise that I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

verses.rationale: Retains collective representation, the specific three-day request, and sacrifice rather than replacing the request with immediate unrestricted departure.
verses.before: And they will listen to your voice, and you and the elders of Israel will go to the king of Egypt and say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, please let us go a three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’
verses.after: The elders will listen to you. Then you and Israel’s elders must go to the king of Egypt and say, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And they will listen to your voice, and you and the elders of Israel shall go to the king of Egypt and say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, please let us go a three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’

verses.rationale: Chooses the except-by-strength construal in context, with the possible not-even-by-strength alternative noted.
verses.before: Yet I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless compelled by a strong hand.
verses.after: But I know the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a strong hand compels him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless compelled by a strong hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the same hand image and divine agency in striking, wonders, and eventual release.
verses.before: So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do in it; after that he will let you go.
verses.after: So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders I will perform there. After that, he will let you go.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do in it; after that he will let you go.

verses.rationale: Keeps favor and the departure’s material consequence without claiming what motivates the Egyptians.
verses.before: I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and when you go, you will not go empty,
verses.after: I will give this people favor in the Egyptians’ eyes, so that when you leave, you will not go empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and when you go, you shall not go empty,

verses.rationale: Keeps women as requesters, the female household relationships, both children’s genders, and plunder; does not turn ask into borrow or add a repayment promise.
verses.before: but each woman will ask of her neighbor, and any woman who lives in her house, for silver and gold jewelry, and for clothing. You will put them on your sons and on your daughters. So you will plunder the Egyptians.”
verses.after: Each woman will ask her neighbor and the woman staying in her house for silver and gold articles and clothing. You will put them on your sons and daughters. In this way you will plunder Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but each woman shall ask of her neighbor, and any woman who lives in her house, for silver and gold jewelry, and for clothing. You shall put them on your sons and on your daughters. So you shall plunder the Egyptians.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ further objection despite the prior assurance that the elders will listen.
verses.before: Then Moses answered, saying, "But look, they will not believe me or listen to my voice, for they will say, 'the LORD has not appeared to you.'"
verses.after: Moses answered, “But what if they do not believe me or listen to me? They may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses answered, saying, "But behold, they will not believe me or listen to my voice, for they will say, 'the LORD has not appeared to you.'"

verses.rationale: Clarifies the speakers and retains the staff before it becomes a sign.
verses.before: The LORD said to him, "What is that in your hand?" He said, "A staff."
verses.after: The LORD asked him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” Moses answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to him, "What is that in your hand?" He said, "A staff."

verses.rationale: Keeps command, action, transformation, and Moses’ fear response in sequence.
verses.before: He said, "Throw it on the ground." So he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it.
verses.after: “Throw it on the ground,” he said. Moses threw it down, and it became a snake. He ran from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And He said, "Throw it on the ground." So he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it.

verses.rationale: Retains the tail and hand details and the reversal of the sign.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand and grasp it by its tail." So he stretched out his hand and caught it, and it became a staff in his hand—
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Reach out your hand and take it by the tail.” Moses reached out and grasped it, and it became a staff in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand and grasp it by its tail." So he stretched out his hand and caught it, and it became a staff in his hand—

verses.rationale: Keeps the explanation as continuing divine speech and preserves the full repeated ancestral identification.
verses.before: that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."
verses.after: “This is so they will believe that the LORD, the God of their ancestors—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily sign and snow comparison without diagnosing the biblical skin-condition term as modern Hansen’s disease.
verses.before: Furthermore, the LORD said to him, "Now put your hand inside your cloak." So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, look, his hand was leprous, like snow.
verses.after: Then the LORD said, “Put your hand inside your cloak.” Moses put it inside his cloak. When he drew it out, his hand had a skin disease, white as snow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Furthermore, the LORD said to him, "Now put your hand inside your cloak." So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous, like snow.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated gesture and complete restoration without supplying a natural mechanism.
verses.before: Then He said, "Put your hand back inside your cloak." So he put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out of his cloak, look, it was restored like his flesh.
verses.after: “Put your hand back inside your cloak,” he said. Moses put it back, and when he drew it out again, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then He said, "Put your hand back inside your cloak." So he put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out of his cloak, behold, it was restored like his flesh.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual voice-of-sign personification that connects believing and listening.
verses.before: "If they will not believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second sign.
verses.after: “If they do not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe the voice of the second.
verses.tsw_comparator: "If they will not believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second sign.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional third sign, Nile origin, dry-ground destination, and literal blood transformation.
verses.before: But if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water that you take from the river will become blood on the ground."
verses.after: If they do not believe even these two signs or listen to you, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water that you take from the river will become blood on the ground."

verses.rationale: Keeps the temporal insistence and heavy-mouth/tongue idiom without diagnosing a particular impairment or making humility the only cause.
verses.before: Then Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I am not a man of words, neither before nor since You have spoken to Your servant. I am slow of speech and slow of tongue."
verses.after: Moses said to the LORD, “Please, my Lord, I have never been a man of words—not before, and not since you began speaking to your servant. My mouth and tongue are slow.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I am not a man of words, neither before nor since You have spoken to Your servant. I am slow of speech and slow of tongue."

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult divine claim and all named capacities using respectful contemporary descriptions, without assigning blame to disabled people.
verses.before: The LORD said to him, "Who has made man's mouth? Or who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
verses.after: The LORD said to him, “Who gave human beings a mouth? Who makes a person unable to speak or deaf, sighted or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to him, "Who has made man's mouth? Or who makes him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily presence promise rather than reducing it to a generic reassurance.
verses.before: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and will teach you what you will speak."
verses.after: Now go. I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and will teach you what you shall speak."

verses.rationale: Renders the idiomatic send-by-whomever-you-will as Moses’ refusal while documenting the literal expression in a note.
verses.before: But he said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."
verses.after: But Moses said, “Please, my Lord, send someone else.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."

verses.rationale: Keeps divine anger, Aaron’s kinship and Levite description, emphatic speaking ability, and his anticipated joy.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and He said, "Is there not Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Moreover, he is coming to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Moses. He said, “What about your brother Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already coming to meet you, and when he sees you, his heart will rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and He said, "Is there not Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Moreover, he is coming to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

verses.rationale: Retains the mouth imagery and makes the plural instruction explicit.
verses.before: You will speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you both what to do.
verses.after: You will speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth and his, and I will teach you both what to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you both what to do.

verses.rationale: Preserves the provocative God/mouth relationship as a functional comparison rather than calling Moses divine by nature.
verses.before: He will speak for you to the people, and he will be as a mouth for you, and you will be to him as God.
verses.after: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your mouth, and you will be as God to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall speak for you to the people, and he will be as a mouth for you, and you will be to him as God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the same staff as the instrument of the forthcoming signs.
verses.before: Take in your hand this staff with which you will do the signs."
verses.after: Take this staff in your hand; with it you will perform the signs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Take in your hand this staff with which you shall do the signs."

verses.rationale: Preserves the request’s stated reason rather than replacing it with the commission; uses Jethro for the short and full name forms within this verse.
verses.before: Then Moses went back to Jethro, his father-in-law, and said to him, "Please let me go back to my brothers in Egypt to see whether they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
verses.after: Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said, “Please let me return to my own people in Egypt and see whether they are still alive.” Jethro answered, “Go in peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses went back to Jethro, his father-in-law, and said to him, "Please let me go back to my brothers in Egypt to see whether they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."

verses.rationale: Keeps the place, command, plural pursuers, and their death without equating them solely with Pharaoh.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life are dead."
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt. All the men who sought your life are dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life are dead."

verses.rationale: Retains plural sons although only one has yet been named, the donkey, and the newly designated staff of God.
verses.before: So Moses took his wife and his sons, set them on a donkey, and returned to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
verses.after: Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and set out for Egypt. He carried the staff of God in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses took his wife and his sons, set them on a donkey, and returned to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in his hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves God’s first-person hardening and refusal sequence without attributing this action to Pharaoh instead.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, "When you go back to Egypt, see that you do all the wonders before Pharaoh that I have put in your hand. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “When you return to Egypt, be sure to perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have put in your hand. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, "When you go back to Egypt, see that you do all the wonders before Pharaoh that I have put in your hand. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.

verses.rationale: Retains collective Israel as the specifically male firstborn image that governs the warning.
verses.before: Then you will say to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the LORD, Israel is my son, my firstborn.
verses.after: Tell Pharaoh, ‘This is what the LORD says: Israel is my son, my firstborn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall say to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the LORD, Israel is my son, my firstborn.

verses.rationale: Preserves the direct killing warning, refusal, and repeated son/firstborn contrast without euphemism.
verses.before: I said to you, "Let my son go that he may serve me." But you have refused to let him go. Look, I will kill your son, your firstborn.'"
verses.after: I told you, “Let my son go so that he may serve me,” but you refused to let him go. Now I will kill your son, your firstborn.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said to you, "Let my son go that he may serve me." But you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn.'"

verses.rationale: Leaves the unnamed threatened person as him rather than silently deciding between Moses and his son; retains the LORD as agent.
verses.before: On the way, at a place where they lodged, the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.
verses.after: At a lodging place along the way, the LORD met him and sought to kill him.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the way, at a place where they lodged, the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps Zipporah’s action, flint, foreskin, ambiguous feet and pronoun, and the opaque blood-bridegroom phrase without inventing an explanation.
verses.before: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son's foreskin and touched it to his feet, saying, "Surely, you are a bridegroom of blood to me."
verses.after: Zipporah took a flint, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched his feet with it. “Truly, you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son's foreskin and touched it to his feet, saying, "Surely, you are a bridegroom of blood to me."

verses.rationale: Retains the pronouns and circumcision explanation while leaving the precise ritual meaning unresolved.
verses.before: So He let him alone. It was then that she said, "A bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.
verses.after: Then he let him alone. It was in connection with circumcision that she said, “A bridegroom of blood.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So He let him alone. It was then that she said, "A bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.

verses.rationale: Preserves Aaron’s own commission and the meeting’s location and affectionate action.
verses.before: The Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.
verses.after: The LORD said to Aaron, “Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.” He went, met him at the mountain of God, and kissed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the message and signs in Moses’ communication to Aaron.
verses.before: Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD with which He had sent him and all the signs that He had commanded him.
verses.after: Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say and all the signs he had commanded him to perform.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD with which He had sent him and all the signs that He had commanded him.

verses.rationale: Retains both leaders and the full elder assembly.
verses.before: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the elders of the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Follows the continuing grammatical subject while noting the possible Moses referent for performed; no unsupported stage directions are added.
verses.before: Aaron spoke all the words that the LORD had spoken to Moses and performed the signs in the sight of the people.
verses.after: Aaron spoke all the words the LORD had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron spoke all the words that the LORD had spoken to Moses and performed the signs in the sight of the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves believed/heard order and attended/seen echoes of the promise and follows Hebrew heard rather than the ancient Greek rejoiced.
verses.before: The people believed, and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel and had seen their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped.
verses.after: The people believed. When they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their suffering, they bowed down in worship.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people believed, and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel and had seen their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped.

comparative_references.scope: Supplemental comparison of bodily signs, speech idioms, ambiguous pronouns, and the heard/rejoiced variant after drafting from Hebrew.

comparative_references.scope: Supplemental grammatical comparison of the divine name, plural serve, and visitation language.

comparative_references.scope: Supplemental comparison of the midwives, birthing supports, households, and Pharaoh’s order.
Every verse in Exodus 1–4, read after drafting independently from the pinned Hebrew.
